spatial_claims.claim: C lies between A and B on line AB, with AC as a segment and CB the remainder
E is on ray from C through B with CE = AC, placing E between C and B (since CE = AC < CB)
D is on ray from E through B with ED = AC, placing D beyond B (since CD = 2AC > CB)
CD = 2*AC and E is the midpoint of CD; D lies on the same side of C as B
AB is cut at C, so II.4 applies: sq(AB) = sq(AC) + sq(CB) + 2*rect(AC,CB)
CD is cut at E (its midpoint), so II.4 applies: sq(CD) = sq(CE) + sq(ED) + 2*rect(CE,ED)
II.1 applied to rect(CB, CD) with CD segmented as CE + ED, requiring E between C and D
CB < CD proved by contradiction; since B and D are on same side of C, B lies between C and D
CD is cut at B (B between C and D), so II.2 applies: rect(CD,CB) + rect(CD,BD) = sq(CD)

configuration_map: All points lie on a single line with ordering A---C---E---B---D. Distances: AC is the base segment, CE = ED = AC, so CD = 2*AC. CB = AC*(sqrt(5)-1) approximately 1.236*AC. Since CE = AC < CB, E falls between C and B. Since CD = 2*AC > CB approximately 1.236*AC, D falls beyond B. Step 6 formally proves CB < CD and concludes B is between C and D. All Book II propositions (II.1, II.2, II.4) are applied to segments with correct betweenness conditions matching this ordering.
pass_reason: The proof operates on points along a single line with a simple ordering A-C-E-B-D. All spatial claims concern collinearity and betweenness, and they are mutually consistent. The critical betweenness claim (B between C and D) is formally proved in Step 6 before being used in Step 7. All applications of Book II propositions match the established point ordering. No angle decompositions, interior/exterior arguments, or complex spatial configurations are involved.
